notes: Hand-verified against the scenario's own arithmetic before comparing to reference-model output. This scenario has no recurring business activity (no revenue/cash expense), so every number traces directly to the two assets' purchase/depreciation/disposal arithmetic — there is no 'steady state' month to assume, each period's figures must be independently derived.

Equipment A: $60,000 / 60 months = $1,000.00/month depreciation. Equipment B: $24,000 / 24 months = $1,000.00/month depreciation. Both purchased 2026-01-01; opening cash 84000.00 − 60000.00 − 24000.00 = 0.00 immediately after.

Equipment B disposal (2026-12-31, 12 months depreciated): accumulated depreciation 12×1000.00 = 12000.00, book value 24000.00 − 12000.00 = 12000.00, gain/loss = proceeds 8000.00 − book value 12000.00 = −4000.00 (a loss). Disposal entry: debit cash 8000.00, debit accumulated_depreciation_equipment_b 12000.00 (zeroing it), debit loss_on_disposal 4000.00; credit equipment_b 24000.00 (zeroing it) — 24000.00 = 24000.00, balances.

2026-12 (December alone, not the full year): depreciation_expense = Equipment A's December depreciation (1000.00) + Equipment B's final, truncated December depreciation (1000.00) = 2000.00; loss_on_disposal 4000.00 (dated the same day); net income = −6000.00. Balance sheet: equipment_b and its accumulated depreciation are both 0.00 (disposed); assets (cash 8000.00 + equipment_a 60000.00 − accumulated_depreciation_a 12000.00) 56000.00 = equity (owner_equity 84000.00 + retained_earnings −28000.00, the full year's net income swept in by the first closing) 56000.00.

2026 (full fiscal year): depreciation_expense 24000.00 (12 months × 1000.00 for each of two assets), loss_on_disposal 4000.00, net income −28000.00. Cash: 84000.00 (opening) − 60000.00 − 24000.00 (both purchases) + 8000.00 (B's disposal proceeds) = 8000.00.

2027-12 and 2027 (full year, identical to each other — Equipment B is gone, nothing else happens all year): only Equipment A depreciates, 1000.00/month × 12 = 12000.00, net income −12000.00 both for the standalone December and for the full year (December's own activity equals the full year's only activity). Cash unchanged at 8000.00 all year. Balance sheet: assets (cash 8000.00 + equipment_a 60000.00 − accumulated_depreciation_a 24000.00, 24 months total) 44000.00 = equity (84000.00 + retained_earnings −40000.00, −28000.00 + −12000.00 across the first two closings) 44000.00.

Equipment A disposal (2028-06-30, 30 months depreciated): accumulated depreciation 30×1000.00 = 30000.00, book value 60000.00 − 30000.00 = 30000.00, gain/loss = proceeds 35000.00 − 30000.00 = +5000.00 (a gain). Disposal entry: debit cash 35000.00, debit accumulated_depreciation_equipment_a 30000.00; credit equipment_a 60000.00, credit gain_on_disposal 5000.00 — both sides 65000.00, balances.

2028-06 (June alone): depreciation_expense = Equipment A's final June depreciation (1000.00, the 30th and last month before disposal); gain_on_disposal 5000.00; net income = 4000.00. Cash: 8000.00 + 35000.00 = 43000.00. current_period_earnings (Jan–Jun 2028, no closing yet that year) = 6 months of A's depreciation (−6000.00) + the June gain (5000.00) = −1000.00. Balance sheet: assets (cash 43000.00, both assets now fully disposed) 43000.00 = equity (84000.00 + retained_earnings −40000.00 + current_period_earnings −1000.00) 43000.00.

2028 (full fiscal year): depreciation_expense 6000.00 (Equipment A, January–June only), gain_on_disposal 5000.00, net income −1000.00 — matches June's standalone figure exactly because all of 2028's activity happened in June. Cash: 8000.00 + 35000.00 = 43000.00 (same as June, since no further activity that year). Balance sheet after the third closing: retained_earnings −41000.00 (−40000.00 + 2028's −1000.00).

2028-12 and 2030 (standalone December 2028, and the full year 2030): zero activity — both assets are gone, there is nothing left to depreciate or dispose of. Net income 0.00, cash flat at 43000.00, balance sheet unchanged (retained_earnings −41000.00 permanently, since 2029/2030 each contribute 0.00).

Cash flow reconciliation note: because cash_flow.py classifies by whole-account period delta (not by individual transaction), a disposal period's operating/investing adjustment lines are coarser than a textbook indirect-method presentation would show (e.g. 2028-06's 'accumulated_depreciation_equipment_a' adjustment is -29000.00 — the net effect of 29 months of depreciation being added back and then the full balance being zeroed out by the disposal in the same delta — rather than a separately broken-out 'depreciation add-back' and 'gain removed from net income' line). The aggregate reconciliation (operating + investing + financing = net change in cash) is exact in every period, which is what this repository's cash flow statement is designed to guarantee — see docs/reference-model.md.
